title: BackgroundService
description: A base class for implementing long-running background tasks in .NET.

data.text: `BackgroundService` is a base class for implementing long-running background tasks in .NET. It is part of the Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting package and is the recommended way to run background work in ASP.NET Core or generic hosts.

data.title: Implementing a Background Service

terms.definition: A base class for implementing background tasks in .NET.

data.title: Graceful Shutdown
data.text: Always respect the `stoppingToken` in your ExecuteAsync loop to allow graceful shutdown.
Scoped Work Inside a Singleton Host

A `BackgroundService` is a singleton, so it cannot inject a scoped service directly. Instead it creates a scope from `IServiceScopeFactory` for each unit of work, which gives it the same per-request lifetime semantics as the web pipeline. `IHostedService` registers alongside the web host, so it starts and stops with the application.

data.title: A background worker with a scope per iteration
Handle the stop signal and exceptions
data.text: The loop must observe `stoppingToken` so shutdown is graceful, or the host waits for the timeout. An unhandled exception inside `ExecuteAsync` stops the worker permanently in some hosts, so wrap each iteration in a `try/catch`, log the failure, and continue. Sleeping without the token is the other common mistake, because it delays shutdown.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: BackgroundService is the standard for background tasks
data.takeaway: Use BackgroundService for reliable long-running tasks in .NET.
